items.prompt:
When the environment changes, species well suited to it may
A) increase in number
B) instantly vanish
C) turn into rocks
D) stop reproducing

A species that cannot survive new conditions may
A) go extinct
B) become a rock
C) always increase
D) change the climate

Over a long time, environmental change can lead to
A) new species emerging
B) no change ever
C) the Sun dimming
D) rocks forming only

steps: New species can emerge over long times.

items.prompt:
In a drier climate, drought-tolerant plants
A) increase while water-loving plants decline
B) die out
C) become water-loving
D) make rain
items.answer: A) increase while water-loving plants decline

items.prompt:
The fossil record shows species appearing and disappearing, which is evidence that
A) environmental change increases, creates, and ends species
B) species never change
C) fossils are fake
D) climate never changes
items.answer: A) environmental change increases, creates, and ends species

steps: The fossil pattern reflects environmental change.

items.prompt:
Extinction is
A) when a species dies out completely
B) when a species increases
C) a new species forming
D) a kind of weather
items.answer: A) when a species dies out completely

steps: Extinction is the complete loss of a species.

items.prompt:
Evaluate: 'Environmental change always causes extinction.' This is
A) too narrow, because change can also increase species and create new ones
B) completely true
C) proof species never change
D) about weather only
items.answer: A) too narrow, because change can also increase species and create new ones

steps: Extinction is only one of three outcomes.

items.prompt:
The three outcomes of environmental change for species are
A) some increase, new species emerge, and others go extinct
B) all die
C) all increase
D) nothing changes
items.answer: A) some increase, new species emerge, and others go extinct

steps: These are the three possible outcomes.
